method: OPEN AND QUOTED, from the RCH Melbourne Clinical Practice Guideline 'Sickle cell disease' (undated page), retrieved 2026-09-23. Every pass claim is machine re-checkable. LICENCE: Free to read but NOT openly licensed -- each page carries '(c) 2026 The Royal Children's Hospital'. Quoted with attribution on the same footing as the 14 RCH guidelines and the Immunisation Handbook guidelines already in this compendium.

claims.claim: **All patients become functionally asplenic** and are at risk of infection with encapsulated organisms (pneumococcus, meningococcus, *Haemophilus*).
claims.source_text: All patients become functionally asplenic and thus at risk for infection particularly by encapsulated organisms (eg pneumococcus, meningococcus, haemophilus).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Sickle cell disease' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Sickle_cell_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Crises may be spontaneous or triggered by** infection, dehydration, hypoxia, or sedatives, local anaesthetics and surgery. SS disease, sickle β-thalassaemia and HbSC disease are all treated the same way.
claims.source_text: Acute crises may occur spontaneously, or may be precipitated by Infection Dehydration Hypoxia Sedatives, local anaesthetics and surgery … There are 3 common types causing sickle disease, all of which are treated the same way: sickle cell anaemia (SS disease) is the most common sickle ß Thalassemia sickle haemoglobin C disease
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Sickle cell disease' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Sickle_cell_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Many presentations need urgent treatment, and discussion with the on-call Haematology Consultant is mandatory.**
claims.source_text: Many of these presentations require urgent treatment, and discussion with the Haematology Consultant on-call is mandatory.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Sickle cell disease' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Sickle_cell_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Investigations:** FBE with reticulocytes · group and crossmatch · blood and urine cultures if febrile · U&E and LFT if jaundiced or dehydrated · consider CXR if febrile with respiratory symptoms. **Compare the spleen with the patient's baseline**; do a neurological examination.
claims.source_text: FBE including reticulocyte count Blood group & cross match Blood and urine cultures if febrile U&E's and LFT's if jaundice or dehydrated Consider chest xray if febrile with respiratory symptoms … Splenic examination – compare to patients baseline Neurological examination
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Sickle cell disease' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Sickle_cell_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Start analgesia promptly and treat pain aggressively.** Mild: paracetamol or ibuprofen. **Moderate to severe: morphine 0.05 mg/kg/dose IV, repeated as necessary**; some benefit from PCA.
claims.source_text: Start analgesics promptly – treat pain aggressively … Mild pain Paracetamol Ibuprofen Moderate to severe pain Morphine 0.05 mg/kg/dose – IV (repeat as necessary) … Some patients may benefit from continuous infusion via PCA (Patient Controlled Analgesia)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Sickle cell disease' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Sickle_cell_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Fluids:** push oral fluids; IV if needed — **bolus 10–20 mL/kg 0.9% saline** if required, then maintenance (Plasma-Lyte 148 + 5% glucose, or 0.9% sodium chloride + 5% glucose).
claims.source_text: Push oral fluids May require IV Fluids May require bolus 10-20 ml/kg 0.9% Saline Maintenance rate (Plasma-Lyte 148 and 5% Glucose OR 0.9% sodium chloride (normal saline) and 5% Glucose)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Sickle cell disease' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Sickle_cell_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Avoid excess fluids after initial resuscitation** (chest crisis risk). **Do not delay IV fluids or analgesia for topical anaesthetic cream.** Transfusion may be needed — discuss with the haematologist.
claims.source_text: Avoid excess fluids after initial resuscitation to reduced risks of chest crisis Do not delay commencement of IV fluids or analgesics for topical anaesthetic cream May require blood transfusion – discuss with haematologist on call
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Sickle cell disease' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Sickle_cell_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Treat all pain initially as vaso-occlusive** — but chest pain with respiratory symptoms may be acute chest syndrome.
claims.source_text: All episodes of pain should be treated initially as vaso-occlusive disease … NB Chest pain may indicate an acute chest syndrome rather than as a vaso-occlusive episode if associated with respiratory symptoms.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Sickle cell disease' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Sickle_cell_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Life-threatening; patients may deteriorate quickly.** Lung infarction with lower respiratory symptoms, hypoxaemia and a new CXR infiltrate — **chest pain and hypoxaemia may be the only signs. Treat chest pain as acute chest syndrome.**
claims.source_text: Usually associated with lower respiratory symptoms, hypoxaemia and a new infiltrate on CXR. Chest pain and hypoxaemia may be the only signs. … Chest pain should be treated as an acute chest syndrome and not simply as a vaso-occlusive crisis. … NB This is a life threatening illness and patients may deteriorate quickly
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Sickle cell disease' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Sickle_cell_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **IV 3rd-generation cephalosporin plus atypical cover (roxithromycin or azithromycin)**; the CXR must not delay treatment. **Oxygen to keep saturation over 96%** or for comfort.
claims.source_text: Consider chest xray – but this should not delay commencement of treatment Commence IV antibiotics – 3rd generation cephalosporin and coverage for atypical organisms (Roxithromycin or Azithromycin) Oxygen to keep O2 sats >96% or for comfort
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Sickle cell disease' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Sickle_cell_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Refer early to PICU** for significant hypoxia or respiratory distress.
claims.source_text: Early referral to PICU for respiratory support if significant hypoxia or respiratory distress
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Sickle cell disease' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Sickle_cell_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Fever: IV 3rd-generation cephalosporin** (add atypical cover if there is a significant respiratory component) and **blood and urine cultures**. Treat co-existing pain as a vaso-occlusive crisis and cough or dyspnoea as acute chest syndrome concurrently.
claims.source_text: NB If pain is also present, then treat as Vaso-occlusive crisis concurrently If cough or dyspnoea is also present look and treat for acute chest syndrome concurrently … Commence IV antibiotics – 3rd generation cephalosporin and consider coverage for atypical organisms (Roxithromycin or Azithromycin) if significant respiratory component Obtain appropriate cultures- blood and urine
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Sickle cell disease' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Sickle_cell_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Definition:** Hb drop of at least 20 g/L below the patient's baseline with an acutely enlarged spleen; often mild–moderate thrombocytopenia; reticulocytes at or above baseline. **Low reticulocytes → consider co-existent aplasia.**
claims.source_text: Splenic sequestion is defined as a haemoglobin drop of at least 20 gm/l below baseline level for that patient with an acutely enlarged spleen. Mild to moderate thrombocytopenia is often present. Reticulocyte count is equal to or greater than patient's usual baseline. Consider co-existent aplastic anaemia if reticulocyte count is low.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Sickle cell disease' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Sickle_cell_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **While waiting for blood, give 0.9% sodium chloride 10–20 mL/kg for hypovolaemia.** Initial transfusion to aim for **Hb 5–6 g/dL** to treat shock (the page adds 'not >3 g/dL').
claims.source_text: While waiting for blood give 0.9% sodium chloride (normal saline) (10-20 ml/kg) to treat hypovolaemia Suggest initial transfusion to aim for Hb of 5-6 g/dL initially to ameliorate shock/haemodynamic instability (not >3 g/dL )
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Sickle cell disease' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Sickle_cell_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Do not raise Hb too far or too fast** — the spleen shrinks and autotransfuses, overshooting Hb with a **risk of stroke from hyperviscosity.** IV 3rd-generation cephalosporin if febrile.
claims.source_text: Do not raise haemoglobin excessively / too quickly as the spleen will shrink and autotransfusion will occur. This will then increase the haemoglobin excessively with increased risk of stroke due to hyperviscosity Commence IV antibiotics if febrile – 3rd generation cephalosporin
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Sickle cell disease' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Sickle_cell_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Aplastic crisis:** Hb below baseline with a markedly reduced reticulocyte count (usually under 1%), usually with acute infection including parvovirus; the spleen may also be enlarged.
claims.source_text: Aplastic crisis is defined as an acute illness associated with haemoglobin below baseline for that patient associated with a substantially decreased reticulocyte count (usually <1%). Usually associated with acute infection including parvovirus. May be associated with enlarged spleen as well
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Sickle cell disease' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Sickle_cell_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **IV plus oral fluids to a total of maintenance. Transfuse red cells if symptomatic or Hb under 5 g/dL — do not increase Hb by more than 3 g/dL.** IV 3rd-generation cephalosporin if febrile.
claims.source_text: Intravenous fluids and oral intake to a total of maintenance Transfuse red blood cells if patient is symptomatic with anaemia or Hb <5 gm/dL (do not increase Hb by >3 g/dL Commence IV antibiotics if febrile – 3rd generation cephalosporin
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Sickle cell disease' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Sickle_cell_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Acute neurological events occur in about 10% of patients with HbSS**, suddenly or as a complication of acute chest syndrome or aplastic crisis.
claims.source_text: Acute neurological events occur in about 10% of patients with Hb SS. Can occur suddenly or as a complication of acute chest syndrome or aplastic crisis
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Sickle cell disease' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Sickle_cell_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Image without delay: MRI is the modality of choice; if unavailable, CT with NO contrast** (hyperviscosity risk worsens the neurological state).
claims.source_text: Obtain CT without contrast to exclude bleed if concerns regarding stroke or MRI if available without delay … MRI is the modality of choice Or if not available CT (NO CONTRAST as risk of hyperviscosity will worsen neurological state)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Sickle cell disease' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Sickle_cell_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Transfusion is required:** options include initial simple transfusion to **Hb 10 g/dL**, then **red cell exchange** (in ICU acutely).
claims.source_text: Transfusion support will be required, options include initial simple transfusion to Hb 10 g/dL followed by Red Cell Exchange (performed in ICU in acute setting)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Sickle cell disease' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Sickle_cell_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Two forms:** stuttering episodes of 2–4 hrs (often recurrent, may precede a severe episode) and **severe attacks over 4 hrs, which can cause impotence.** Most common in adolescence.
claims.source_text: Most common in adolescent years. Occurs in 2 forms stuttering episodes which last 2-4 hrs but are often recurrent and may precede a severe episode severe attack lasting longer than 4 hrs and can result in impotence.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Sickle cell disease' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Sickle_cell_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Empty the bladder (catheterise if needed); moderate exercise, bath or shower. Do NOT use ice.** Start hydration, oxygen, analgesia and urinary alkalinisation as soon as possible.
claims.source_text: Encourage emptying of the bladder: catheterise if unable to empty bladder Simple measures – moderate exercise, take a bath or shower Do not use ICE Hydration, oxygen, analgesia and alkanization of the urine should be commenced as soon as possible
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Sickle cell disease' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Sickle_cell_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Priapism over 4 hours is a urological emergency** — consult General Surgery (Urology) and the on-call haematologist.
claims.source_text: Priapism lasting more than 4 hours can result in ischaemia and is a urological emergency. Consult General Surgery (Urology) and on-call Haematologist.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Sickle cell disease' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Sickle_cell_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23
